messages:
ash: us-west2 dedicated pool is showing mass pod evictions and queue depth spike. pods OOM'ing (nv/llm-serve) — traffic is starting to fallback to hosted. anyone oncall?

leo: I'm on it. seeing a pattern: KV cache growth per-request, memory footprints ~62GB on 80GB GPUs then eviction. autoscaler didn't add nodes fast enough, cooldown=600s.

infra-bot: Alert: dedicated-pool-usw2 - eviction-rate 0.28/s, scale_event: suppressed due to cooldown

maria: Ok let's do short-term mitigation: shift low-priority org weights to hosted and drain 3 nodes for reboot to clear cache.

sahil: cost note — hosted absorb will bump spend but ok for <3h. anyone have command to shift weights?

ash: running routing update: `curl -XPOST https://router.internal/weights -d '{ "pool":"us-west2", "low_priority":0.9 }'` -- applying now

infra-bot: Weights update accepted, new low_priority hosted weight=0.9

leo: Draining nodes now: `kubectl drain node/usw2-ded-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> started

ops-sre: Creating incident and paging infra-oncall.

ops-sre: incident created INC-2026-342, paging infra-oncall

oncall: acknowledged, attaching runbook: https://runbooks.internal/dedicated-oom

maria: Observed that scale-down cooldown was set to 10m and scale-up threshold too aggressive; propose tune to faster scale-up and bump min replicas to 15 for this pool.

sahil: Agreed. Also opening ticket to add KV cache LRU cap in runtime so single org can't blow memory.

ash: Failover looks stable, hosted taking ~82% of low-priority requests. Latency unchanged for high-priority. Continuing to monitor.

leo: Post-drain node reclaimed 1.2TB ephemeral and restarted runtime, memory footprints back to expected. Evictions dropping.

infra-bot: Alert cleared: eviction-rate below threshold for 5m

maria: Follow-ups: 1) change autoscaler ramp to 2x for bursts, 2) add QoS cap on cache, 3) incident postmortem tomorrow 10am.

ash: thanks everyone — keep updates in thread. :thumbsup:
